why.title: Four principles behind how we work

i1.title: AI-native engineering
i1.text: AI is part of how we analyse requirements, write and review code, test and document, not an add-on service. Engineers remain responsible for every result.

i2.title: Forward Deployed Engineer mindset
i2.text: Our engineers work close to your team, learn the business context, investigate the real problem and propose better options, instead of only implementing tickets. It is the standard we train every engineer towards.

i3.title: Professionalism and ownership
i3.text: Clear communication, honest status reporting, disciplined execution and continuous learning. When something goes wrong, we say so early and fix it.

i4.title: Customer value first
i4.text: We recommend what fits your situation, including a simpler or non-AI solution when that serves you better.

flow.aria: How we work: from your business challenge through discover, design, build, validate and operate, to business impact. AI assists every step; engineers own the outcome.

s1.title: Discover

s2.ai: Reading existing code and specifications to speed up analysis.

s3.title: Design
s3.text: Agree on architecture, scope and the right level of AI, which is sometimes none.

s4.title: Build

s5.title: Validate

s6.title: Operate and improve

bis2.heroTitle: BIS: an AI learning system built on structured Biology knowledge
bis2.heroText: BIS represents Biology as concepts and relations, so that an AI tutor can explain with sources, check understanding and track each learner's progress. Teachers review content before it is used.
bis2.problemText: Most Biology learning still comes as videos, slides and one-way lectures. When a student misunderstands a concept, it is rarely noticed, and teachers cannot tailor explanations to every learner.
bis2.solutionText: BIS represents Biology as concepts, relations, evidence and common misconceptions. On this structure, the AI tutor explains with sources, sets the right practice questions and tracks what each learner has mastered.

f1.title: Structured knowledge
f1.text: Concepts, relations, evidence and misconceptions are represented explicitly, with a change history.

f2.title: AI tutor that shows sources
f2.text: Answers are based on approved material and show where they come from.

f3.title: Practice matched to understanding
f3.text: Questions are linked to concepts and misconceptions, so wrong answers show where a learner is stuck.

f4.title: Mastery tracking
f4.text: Mastery is recorded per concept to suggest what to practise next.

f5.title: Teacher review
f5.text: AI only writes drafts. A Biology teacher reviews and approves them before anything is used.

f6.title: Trustworthy material
f6.text: Only self-written or openly licensed material is used, and every change is recorded.

bis2.todayText: The current prototype includes a student portal with practice questions, a source-cited AI tutor, mastery tracking and an admin review workflow. Content is still draft and is being prepared for review by Biology teachers.

road1.title: Now
road1.text: Working prototype, first Biology scope: cell biology, molecular biology and genetics.

road2.title: Next
road2.text: Teacher-reviewed content, real user accounts, and a pilot with advanced high-school Biology and competition preparation.

road3.title: Later
road3.text: More subjects and levels, such as university and vocational education. This is a plan, not a delivered scope.

q1.title: Who is BIS for?
q1.text: Our first focus is advanced high-school Biology in Vietnam, including competition preparation. Teachers, schools and learning programmes are our target audience.

q2.title: Is BIS available now?
q2.text: BIS is an experimental prototype. If you are a teacher or school interested in a pilot or in giving feedback, please email us.

q3.title: How do you keep AI answers accurate?
q3.text: The tutor answers from approved source passages and shows citations. AI-written questions stay as drafts until a Biology teacher approves them.

q4.title: Where does the content come from?
q4.text: We use content we write ourselves or sources with open licences. Copyrighted textbooks are not used without permission.

bis2.ctaText: Teachers, schools and partners are welcome to ask about a pilot or share feedback.

aab.name: AAB
aab.text: Business process automation: BPMN 2.0 processes on Camunda, AI agents for defined tasks, and approvals through Microsoft 365.

aab.heroTitle: AAB: automate business processes with BPMN and AI agents
aab.heroText: AAB runs business processes modelled in BPMN 2.0 on the Camunda workflow engine. AI agents carry out defined tasks in the process, such as classifying requests and extracting data from documents. Approvals go to people through Microsoft 365.
aab.problemTitle: Processes buried in email and spreadsheets
aab.problemText: Many processes still depend on email, files and people's memory. Approvals stall, documents are re-entered, and no one can see where a case is stuck.
aab.solutionText: The process is a BPMN model: every step, decision and handover is visible and versioned. AI agents are called only at defined steps, and where accountability matters their output goes to a person for review before the process continues.

c1.title: BPMN 2.0 process on Camunda
c1.text: Camunda executes the model: it keeps the state of every case, handles timers and deadlines, and records each execution step.

c2.title: AI agents as process tasks
c2.text: Agents run as service tasks: classifying requests, extracting data from documents and drafting replies, using your knowledge and tools.

c3.title: Microsoft 365
c3.text: Requests come in, and approvals and notifications go out, through Microsoft 365, so people keep working in the tools they use today.

c4.title: Human approval
c4.text: AI proposes, people decide. Steps that need accountability are user tasks with a named approver, and every action is recorded.

aab.whereText: AAB is in development. Drawing on our BPMN and workflow project experience, we are building its workflow core on Camunda.

q1.title: What does AAB do?
q1.text: It automates business processes. Processes are modelled in BPMN 2.0 and executed on a workflow engine; AI agents carry out defined steps such as classifying, extracting and drafting.

q2.title: Is AAB available now?
q2.text: AAB is in development. If you have a process you would like to automate, email us to talk about it.

q3.title: Does AI replace people?
q3.text: No. AI handles preparation work, people approve and decide, and the system records what happened.

aab.ctaText: Tell us how it works today. We will reply by email.

q4.title: Where is AI used, and where not?
q4.text: AI is used only in defined tasks such as classification, extraction and drafting. Routing, deadlines and approvals are defined in the BPMN model and executed by the workflow engine, not decided by AI.

aab.exampleTitle: How a request moves through an AAB process
aab.exampleSub: A simplified process in BPMN notation. Real processes are modelled together with the customer.

diagram.alt: BPMN diagram. A request arrives and starts the process. An AI agent classifies the request and extracts data, then drafts a reply. A reviewer checks the draft. If it is approved, the reply is sent and the case closes; if it is rejected, the draft is revised.
diagram.legend: Message start event · Service task (AI agent, system) · User task (person) · Exclusive gateway · End event
diagram.s1: A request arrives (message start event) and starts the process.
diagram.s2: An AI agent classifies the request and extracts data (service task).
diagram.s3: An AI agent drafts a reply (service task).
diagram.s4: A reviewer checks the draft (user task).
diagram.s5: Exclusive gateway: if approved, the reply is sent (service task); if rejected, the draft is revised.
diagram.s6: The case closes and its history is kept (end event).

founderMsg.title: Building an AI-native engineering company
founderMsg.quote: Technology creates its greatest value when the engineers building it understand the business problem behind it.
founderMsg.p1: I trained in the HEDSPI programme at Hanoi University of Science and Technology, a Vietnam–Japan IT engineering programme supported by JICA. Alongside the technical curriculum, we studied the Japanese language and Japanese working culture in depth. After graduating, I began working on software for Japanese clients in 2011, and over the following years moved from writing code to leading projects and delivery, across ERP, embedded systems, business workflow, healthcare and AI. One lesson kept repeating: technology creates its greatest value when the engineers building it understand the business problem behind it.
founderMsg.p2: Too often, outsourcing turns engineers into ticket-takers. The specification arrives, the code is delivered, and nobody asks whether it solves the real problem. That model breaks down when a customer's challenge is unclear, spans several systems, or changes as the work progresses.
founderMsg.p3: I founded Brisasoft in 2024 because AI is changing how software is designed, built and operated, and engineering teams must change with it. We use AI throughout our work so that engineers can spend more of their time on what matters: understanding the context, challenging assumptions and exploring better solutions.
founderMsg.p4: Our ambition is for every Brisasoft engineer to develop a Forward Deployed Engineer mindset: technical depth, business understanding, practical problem-solving and close collaboration with customers. We are building that capability step by step, and it is the standard we hold ourselves to.
founderMsg.p5: AI helps us work more effectively, but it does not replace engineering judgement, responsibility, or the trust built between people. We value professionalism, dedication, transparency and continuous improvement, and we will tell you plainly when a simpler or non-AI solution is the better choice.
founderMsg.p6: We want to be more than a software vendor: a dependable technology partner that helps you turn business challenges into practical, sustainable solutions. Thank you for considering Brisasoft.

quality.title: How we keep delivery predictable
quality.sub: Practices we apply on every engagement, scaled to the size of the project.

q1.title: Requirements clarification
q1.text: Open questions are tracked in a shared Q&A list until each one is answered.

q2.title: Technical design
q2.text: Architecture and specification documents are reviewed before development starts.

q3.title: Code review
q3.text: Every change is reviewed by another engineer. AI-assisted review is an extra check, not a replacement.

q4.title: Testing
q4.text: Unit, integration and acceptance testing, with test cases traceable to requirements.

q5.title: Security checks
q5.text: Dependency checks, no secrets in source code, and access limited to what each environment needs.

q6.title: Documentation
q6.text: Specifications, operating notes and decisions kept up to date as the system changes.

q7.title: Progress reporting
q7.text: Regular reports on progress, risks and open issues, in a format agreed with you.

q8.title: Knowledge transfer
q8.text: Handover material and sessions so your team can operate and extend the system.
